scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PM-FME)
overview: The Pradhan Mantri Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PM-FME) Scheme is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) to provide financial, technical, and business support for the upgradation of existing micro food processing enterprises. It aims to enhance the competitiveness of individual micro enterprises, promote the 'One District One Product' (ODOP) approach, and support the formalization of the sector through credit-linked subsidies, seed capital, and capacity building. The scheme covers various components including individual micro enterprises, groups (FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives), and common infrastructure.
objectives: Provide credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of eligible project cost with a maximum of Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for upgradation or setting up of new units for individual micro enterprises

Provide credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of eligible project cost with a maximum of Rs. 3.00 Crore for groups (FPOs/FPCs/Cooperatives/SHGs and their federation/Govt. Agencies) for establishing food processing lines with common infrastructure/value chain/incubation centers
Provide seed capital @ Rs. 40,000/- per member of SHG for working capital and purchase of small tools, maximum upto Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG
Provide 50% financial grant for Branding and Marketing Support to groups of FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives or a SPV of micro food processing enterprises
Provide training on Food Processing Entrepreneurship Development Programme to PMFME beneficiaries under the Capacity Building component
Promote the One District One Product (ODOP) approach to reap benefits of scale in procurement, availing common services, and marketing of products
Support the formalization and mainstreaming of unorganized home-based or micro food processing units
Enhance competitiveness and promote value addition in the micro food processing sector
eligibility: Individual Micro Enterprises: Individuals, Proprietorship, Partnership, FPOs, NGOs, Cooperatives, SHGs, Pvt. Ltd. Co. would be provided credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost with a maximum of Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for upgradation or setting up of new units. Groups: The Groups - FPOs/FPCs/Cooperatives/SHG and its federation/Govt. Agencies - established or propose to establish food processing line along with common infrastructure/Value chain/incubation centers would be provided credit linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost with a maximum of Rs. 3.00 Crore. Seed Capital for SHGs: Seed capital @ Rs. 40,000/- per member of SHG for working capital and purchase of small tools maximum upto 4 Lakhs per SHG. Marketing & Branding: The scheme provides 50% financial grant for Branding and Marketing Support to groups of FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives or a SPV of micro food processing enterprises to promote their existing or proposed brands to market their processed food products under the scheme.
benefits: Financial benefits include credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of eligible project cost (max Rs. 10.0 lakhs for individual units, max Rs. 3.00 Crore for groups), seed capital @ Rs. 40,000/- per SHG member (max Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG), and 50% financial grant for branding and marketing support for groups. Non-financial benefits include capacity building through training on Food Processing Entrepreneurship Development Programme, support under the One District One Product (ODOP) approach for value chain development and alignment of support infrastructure, and assistance in formalization of micro food processing enterprises.
financial_support: The scheme provides credit-linked capital subsidy @35% of the eligible project cost. For individual micro enterprises (Individual/Proprietorship/Partnership/FPOs/NGOs/Cooperatives/SHGs/Pvt. Ltd. Co.), the maximum subsidy is Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit. For groups (FPOs/FPCs/Cooperatives/SHG and its federation/Govt. Agencies), the maximum subsidy is Rs. 3.00 Crore. Seed capital for SHGs is provided as grant @ Rs. 40,000/- per member for working capital and purchase of small tools, maximum upto Rs. 4 Lakhs per SHG. The scheme also provides 50% financial grant for branding and marketing support to groups of FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives or a SPV of micro food processing enterprises.
application_process: The application process is not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence. However, based on the scheme structure, applicants would typically need to: 1. Identify eligibility under individual micro enterprise, group, or SHG components. 2. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) as per guidelines. 3. Apply through the designated portal or nodal agency. 4. Submit required documents including DPR, identity proof, bank details, etc. 5. Await sanction and disbursement of subsidy through credit-linked mechanism. 6. Utilize funds for project implementation as per approved DPR. 7. Submit utilization reports and comply with monitoring requirements.
required_documents: Certificate of Incorporation/Registration (for companies, LLPs, partnerships)
Term loan sanction letter from bank/financial institution (if applicable)
SHG federation/SRLM/SULM recommendation (for seed capital component)
Branding and marketing plan (for marketing grant component)
caveats: Subsidy is credit-linked and released in installments based on term loan disbursement and project progress
Promoter's contribution (minimum 10%) and term loan (maximum 55%) are required as part of the means of finance
Land development, building, and civil construction costs are not eligible for subsidy under the scheme
The scheme does not cover working capital requirements directly (except seed capital for SHGs)
Beneficiaries must comply with monitoring, reporting, and utilization requirements post-sanction
The subsidy amount is capped at Rs. 10.0 lakhs per unit for individual enterprises and Rs. 3.00 Crore for groups regardless of actual eligible project cost
Seed capital for SHGs is provided as grant to SHG Federation by SRLM/SULM through SNA for loan to SHG members
Marketing and branding support is limited to 50% financial grant for groups only
